First release of Storyworks, a local-first desktop app for writing books, screenplays and game scripts. Everything is stored as plain JSON files in a folder you choose; nothing is sent anywhere. English and Polish UI.

## What's in v1.0.0

**Books**
- Manuscript editor: parts, chapters and scenes with stable paragraph IDs, footnotes, comments, images, scene status and synopsis, corkboard, inbox, focus mode.
- Timelines with branching events and a custom calendar; link any paragraph to an event.
- Rules of your world, and a codex of characters, places and items with relationships, groups, dated states and who-knows-what-since-when.
- Consistency checks (no AI): dates out of order, knowledge used too early, appearances after a final state, broken links and more. Each check can be switched off.
- Export to PDF and DOCX with optional dramatis personae, glossary and chronology; import from Markdown and plain text with a preview.

**Screenplays**
- Element editor with Tab flow, scene numbers, page count and runtime.
- Export to PDF, Word and Fountain; Fountain import and paste.

**Game scripts**
- Speaker lines with stable IDs, variables, branching conversations with conditions and variable changes, story map, routes and play-through.
- Game document: overview, mechanics (status, parameters, links to variables, items, beats and codex entries) and glossary.
- Game checks (dead ends, unreachable nodes, undefined variables, broken mechanic links and more); game JSON and CSV export; document export to PDF, DOCX and Markdown.

**Everywhere**
- Snapshots and automatic backups with plain-word history and restore; search and quick switcher; writing goals and stats; spellcheck (English, Polish, your own words).
- Single-writer lock, external-change detection, crash recovery and a local diagnostics log with no manuscript text.
- Light and dark themes, UI zoom, rebindable shortcuts, keyboard-operable UI, a guided tour per project kind, and sample projects (book, screenplay, game script) from the Welcome screen.

## Install

Linux: `.deb` or `.AppImage`. Windows: `.msi` or `.exe`. The installers are **not code-signed**, so Windows SmartScreen warns on first run: choose **More info → Run anyway**.

## Known limits

- Some accessibility items are deferred: a roving-tabindex editor toolbar, a live-region announcement of the screenplay element type, nested dialog roles. See `docs/review/a11y-m11b.md`.
- A conversation canvas with about 300 nodes paints in roughly 330 ms.
- Installers are built by CI; real-window behaviour on each platform is checked by hand before publishing.
